english.title: Publish advert re - indecent photograph / pseudo-photograph of a child
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) published an advertisement likely to be understood as conveying that the advertiser distributed or showed indecent

(A)_[photographs]_
(B)_[pseudo-photographs]_

of children or intended to do so
english.legislation: Contrary to section 1(1)(d) and 6 of the Protection of Children Act 1978.

investigatoraction.description: Attracts liability for entry on sex offenders register
Consider an application for a sexual harm prevention order after conviction

DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) The consent of the Director of Public Prosecutions is required.
(ii) 'Child' means a person under 16 (sec 7(6)) but see section 7(8) for proviso in relation to pseudo- photographs.
(iii) This offence is included in Schedule 3 to the Sexual Offences Act 2003. Therefore a person convicted or cautioned for this offence must comply with the notification requirements of Part 2 of that Act.
(iv) This offence is included in Schedule 2 to the Sex Offenders Act 1997. Therefore a person committing this offence outside the United Kingdom may in certain circumstances be prosecuted for that offence in England, Wales or Northern Ireland.
(v) The penalty on indictment was increased from three to ten years by section 41 of the Criminal Justice and Court Services Act 2000.
(vi) Please refer to the extensive Notes in relation to this offence which are attached to the legal topic document covering section 1 of the Protection of Children Act 1978.
(vii) Sections 1A and 1B of the Protection of Children Act 1978 provides defences to the offence in specified circumstances.

other.penalty:
SUMMARY: Six months imprisonment and / or a fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
INDICTMENT: Ten years imprisonment.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
